title: Behavior induction
body:
For example in #173, beyond learning rubrics it would be great if the agent can learn from the user behavior and create proper updates to the infra as well? 

@sepo-agent /answer what do u think?

nodes.body:
Yes, I think this is the right direction, but I would make it a **proposal-and-approval loop**, not silent infra mutation.

The current split is good: [`agent/rubrics`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.agent/docs/architecture/rubrics.md#L3-L8) captures normative user/team preferences, while [`agent/memory`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.agent/docs/architecture/memory.md#L3-L5) captures agent/project continuity. The missing third category is: **behavior signals that imply the infra itself should change**.

Example from #173: if repeated orchestrator runs drift into patchy scope expansion, that is not just a rubric like “prefer canonical design.” It is evidence that the orchestrator needs a structured reflection gate. That should become an infra proposal, then an implementation PR.

I would implement it this way:

1. Add an `infra_gap` / `behavior_observation` output path to the existing learning flow.
   - `agent-rubrics-update.yml` already learns from merged PR conversations and writes only dedicated rubrics via [`rubrics_mode_override: enabled`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.github/workflows/agent-rubrics-update.yml#L85-L107).
   - `agent-memory-pr-closed.yml` already records durable lessons after PR close via [`memory_mode_override: enabled`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.github/workflows/agent-memory-pr-closed.yml#L80-L103).
   - Both can identify “this is not a rubric/memory note; this is an infra gap.”

2. Add a dedicated workflow, probably `Agent / Self Improvement / Propose`.
   - It should read memory, rubrics, mirrored GitHub artifacts, and recent PR/issue behavior.
   - It should produce a GitHub issue or discussion comment with:
     - observed behavior pattern
     - evidence links
     - affected infra files
     - proposed fix
     - risk level
     - suggested implementation route

3. Keep code changes behind explicit approval at first.
   - The proposal can say: “Recommended next step: `/implement` this infra update.”
   - Existing routes can then do the actual code change.
   - This avoids letting a scheduled learning pass rewrite workflows or orchestration logic without a human checkpoint.

4. Later, allow opt-in auto-PR creation for low-risk infra updates.
   - For example: prompt wording, docs, small deterministic validation, missing tests.
   - Workflow/orchestrator policy changes should stay approval-gated until this proves reliable.

This fits the current architecture because [`run-agent-task`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L229-L263) already has policy-gated memory/rubrics mounting, and commits are already separately gated for memory and rubrics via [`Commit memory edits`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L339-L355) and [`Commit rubric edits`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L366-L402). We can reuse that pattern instead of blending infra changes into rubric learning.

For #173 specifically, the first behavior-induced infra proposal would be: add a structured orchestrator reflection checkpoint. The orchestrator planner already runs in [`agent-orchestrator.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.github/workflows/agent-orchestrator.yml#L145-L184), but today the handoff action space is still basically `implement | review | fix-pr` as defined in [`handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L3-L4). The reflection gate would teach the planner when to stop, split, or ask for human design input instead of continuing the loop.

Recommended next step: implement a scoped `self-improvement-propose` workflow that only opens proposals. After that lands, we can decide which proposal classes are safe enough to auto-open draft PRs.
